finding.claim: Ruby exceptions raised by user collation comparators (and authorizer, busy handler, trace callbacks) are not wrapped in rb_protect, so they longjmp through sqlite3_step/sqlite3_prepare, leaving the db mutex locked and VDBE state corrupted (DoS / connection deadlock).
finding.source: Attacker-stored row bytes reaching a user collation (ORDER BY col COLLATE x), or attacker SQL reaching the authorizer, causing the app callback to raise (e.g. ArgumentError on invalid UTF-8).
finding.sink: rb_funcall(comparator, "compare") inside rb_comparator_func, invoked from sqlite3_step which holds db->mutex.

trace.note: sqlite3_step acquires db mutex and executes the statement
rb_comparator_func invoked by SQLite during sort
rb_funcall without rb_protect; exception longjmps past sqlite3_mutex_leave

finding.guards_checked: rb_protect used for scalar functions (database.c:581) and aggregators (aggregator.c:143,161) but not for collation (database.c:839), authorizer (database.c:738), busy handler (database.c:365), or trace (database.c:328).

finding.claim: On 64-bit builds, Ruby Bignum values in int64 range (and out-of-range ones) returned from user SQL functions fall through to sqlite3_result_double, losing precision. Similarly statement.c binds out-of-int64 bignums as double silently.
finding.source: Integer values in [2^62, 2^63) or outside int64, from a bound parameter or from a user SQL function computing a 64-bit ID/hash/permission value.
finding.sink: sqlite3_result_double (database.c:521) and sqlite3_bind_double (statement.c:293) storing the value as REAL, which changes SQL equality/range results.

trace.note: case T_BIGNUM block; bignum_to_int64 only compiled under SIZEOF_LONG < 8, so empty on 64-bit
bind T_BIGNUM: in-range handled, out-of-range falls through

finding.guards_checked: bignum_to_int64 used on bind path for in-range values only and only on 32-bit function-result path; no rejection of out-of-range values anywhere.

finding.claim: step() treats any non-nil rb_errinfo() as a pending callback exception. Inside a rescue/ensure block, $! is non-nil, so step executes the statement, then clears $! and raises the unrelated outer exception, discarding the step result.
finding.source: Precondition: application calls stmt.step inside a rescue or ensure clause while an exception is in flight.
finding.sink: sqlite3_step executes the statement (including writes); rb_set_errinfo(Qnil) and rb_exc_raise re-raise the stale exception.

trace.note: sqlite3_step runs the statement, side effects committed
rb_errinfo() != Qnil true because of enclosing rescue
stale exception re-raised; step result lost

finding.guards_checked: Only a nil check on rb_errinfo(); no check that the exception originated from a callback during this step.

finding.claim: statement_timeout= ignores the configured ms value: the deadline is set to the current time on the first progress callback, so any statement running past about 2000 VM ops is interrupted regardless of the setting. Fail-closed, not an attacker bypass.
finding.sink: Progress handler returning 1 to abort the statement with SQLITE_INTERRUPT.

trace.note: stmt_timeout stored, never read by handler
second callback: now is after deadline, return 1 (interrupt)
prepare clears deadline, so cycle repeats per statement

finding.guards_checked: None; the deadline is not computed as start + stmt_timeout.
